title: AuthZ contract playbook & pricing experiment for SAML SSO and RBAC commitments
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Purpose: define a repeatable contract playbook and an A/B pricing experiment that treats SAML SSO and RBAC as optional add-ons vs. as included enterprise commitments. Goal is to measure churn, time-to-close, and legal negotiation time when SSO/RBAC are explicitly contract line-items with defined SLAs and responsibilities.

Background: Customers frequently include SSO (SAML) and role-based access controls in security questionnaires or require them in contract attachments. Legal wants a clear set of commitment levels (Basic, Managed, and Certified) mapped to pricing tiers. Engineering needs scoping clarity (SAML metadata rotation, SCIM/RBAC APIs, audit log retention). This ticket codifies packaging options and runs a pricing experiment with two pilot cohorts.

Decisions made so far:
- Packaging model: three options proposed: (1) Basic Enterprise: SSO (SAML) supported via self-managed metadata + org-level RBAC (admin, dev, viewer) included; (2) Managed Auth add-on: we operate SSO metadata rotation and SCIM sync for a monthly fee; (3) Certified Security add-on: contractual SLA for audit log retention, KMS/HSM attestations and custom RBAC roles with org-wide mapping.
- Pricing experiment: run a randomized offering to inbound enterprise leads over 8 weeks. Cohort A gets Basic Enterprise included at list price; Cohort B receives Basic + Managed Auth at a 15% discount (annual commit), Cohort C sees Basic + Managed Auth + Certified as an explicit add-on with separately scoped pricing.
- Contract language: standard clause templates drafted by Legal in Confluence (link below). Key ask: limit RBAC contractual commitment to role mapping surface area (max 20 custom roles) unless Certified package purchased to prevent open-ended engineering scope.

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Engineering effort vs. sales velocity: committing to managed SSO operations increases time to close but reduces post-sale integration work for customers and support burden.
- SLA granularity: should RBAC be covered by a 99.9% availability commitment or excluded from platform uptime SLAs? Legal prefers exclusion unless Certified package purchased.
- Security questionnaires: when we mark SAML/RBAC as "supported and configurable" vs. "contractual commitment" customers interpret differently, causing negotiation delays.

Progress updates and artifacts:
- 2025-10-02: Draft PRD created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/AuthZ+Playbook+2025. (owner: Aisha Rahman)
- 2025-10-04: Engineering scoping doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/eng/authz-scope (ENG owners: Priya Nair, Chris Gomez). Estimated implementation effort for Managed Auth: 6 sprint-weeks.
- 2025-10-06: Legal template bank added: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LegalTemplatesAuthZ (LEGAL owner: Marta Ivanov).
- 2025-10-10: GitHub spike PR for SAML metadata rotation & SCIM endpoints: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4721 (linked to ENG-4930).
- 2025-10-12: Pricing experiment plan (A/B/C cohorts) published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/AuthZ+Pricing+Experiment+Plan. Metrics: time-to-close, margin, support tickets in first 90 days, legal negotiation hours.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- Contract templates approved by Legal and Security (LEGAL-27 closed).
- Engineering provides an implementation ETA and a feature flag to turn Managed Auth on/off per-customer (ENG-4930 toggles).
- Pilot with two customers executed (Acme Health and FinServe) and metrics collected for at least 30 days.
- Pricing experiment launched and instrumented in Salesforce/HubSpot with conversion & negotiation time tracked.

Next steps (owner):
- Diego Morales: finalize pricing levels and create SKU lines for Managed Auth and Certified Security (due 2025-10-20).
- Priya Nair / Chris Gomez: deliver engineering spike results and a risk assessment for scaling metadata rotation (deliverable due 2025-10-18).
- Marta Ivanov (Legal): provide redlines for the Basic vs Certified clause and confirm whether RBAC role limits are enforceable (due 2025-10-22).
- PM to recruit two pilot customers and agree scope: onboarding checklist, SLAs, and support playbooks.

Longer-term outcomes we will evaluate:
- Does including Managed Auth as part of an enterprise commit increase ARR and reduce churn vs selling it as an add-on?
- What is the incremental engineering and support cost per customer for Managed Auth and Certified bundles?
- Should RBAC capabilities be productized (self-serve role builder) to avoid contract-scoped customizations?
